evidence.why_not_priced: It mostly is priced: a guide beat is the pattern everyone following the name has seen twice. What is not priced is the size of the beat; if the market expected a larger beat the stock would not have drifted -9% in 20 days into the print.
evidence.independence: Q2 beat confirmed in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/382211/agora-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results) and in Xinhua's report 'above the top of the guidance range' (https://www.news.cn/finance/20260814/9553c320e1074d32a8344f0c582f8d2e/c.html).

evidence.text: The stock was sold down into the print: -7.0% over 5 days and -8.9% over 20 days, mostly on 2026-11-12 (-5.21%) and 2026-11-13 (-3.18%), with no company-specific news found; spot $3.98 sits 33-41% below the stale mean analyst targets of $5.90-6.80, so the bar the market holds going in is lower than at the Q2 print (stock then ~$4.5-4.7).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a run-up and was sold (-3.93%); Q3 2025, after a weak period, was bought +9.06%. Two cases, opposite setups, consistent with a lower bar helping.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the price; what may not be priced is that it has no company cause found. Unexplained microcap drawdowns are weak evidence either way.

evidence.text: On its last print (Q2 2026, 2026-08-13) Agora beat the top of its guide by $0.4M and guided Q3 to an accelerating 15.8-18.6% growth, yet the stock fell -3.93% the next session and drifted a reported -11.3% afterwards, showing the shareholder base does not pay for guide beats while gross margin is falling (63.7% vs 66.8% YoY) and operating income is still negative (-2.4% margin).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a reaction-function item, not a fact the market lacks: it says a repeat of the Q2 pattern (beat, margin down, small op loss) is likely to be sold again. If the market already discounted it, the stock would be flat into the print rather than having drifted only after the last one.
evidence.independence: Margin and op-loss figures from a different summary (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/agora/earnings/2026-q2-summary); the -3.93% from the sealed baseline.

evidence.why_not_priced: The filings are public (Form 4s are new for this foreign private issuer in 2026), but no wire or aggregator covered the purchases; a ~8%-of-volume bid that continues through the window (10b5-1, not blacked out) is a mechanical support for a thin ADS on a negative reaction. If priced, the stock would not have fallen 8% in two sessions while he bought.
evidence.independence: Start of buying in the 2026-10-13 Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1802883/000119312526419691/ownership.xml); plan terms in the 2026-06-01 release (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/01/3304332/0/en/Agora-Inc-Announces-Management-Share-Purchase-Plan.html). next_guide.basis: The 2026-09-16 Q3 raise left the FY guide unchanged, so the implied Q4 fell to ~+16% (derived below) against H1 +32% and Q3 +21%. Amer has raised the FY guide at every 2026 print (May, August). Anta reported a September and Golden Week recovery in China. A raise is therefore the likely direction; its size against a street already at the top of the range is the open question.

evidence.text: Leaving the FY guide unchanged on 2026-09-16 while raising Q3 implies Q4 revenue growth of only about +16%, against +32% in H1 and +21% guided for Q3. The arithmetic: FY2025 revenue $6.566B x 1.24 = ~$8.14B; H1 2026 = H1 2025 ($1.474B Q1 + $1.236B Q2 = $2.71B) x 1.321 = ~$3.58B; Q3 at +21% on $1.756B = ~$2.125B; implied Q4 = ~$2.44B against Q4 2025 of ~$2.10B. A FY raise of at least the Q3 flow-through (+$20-40M, ~0.3-0.5pt) is close to mechanical, and the company raised the FY at the May and August prints. The street's FY EPS of $1.30 already sits at the top of the $1.27-1.30 guide, so a raise is expected; how far above the mechanical step it goes decides the reaction.

evidence.text: The FY27 street ($7.43 EW, $7.50 TIKR) sits above the floor of the company's only FY27 guide. 'Double-digit adj EPS growth excluding the 53rd week' off ~$6.64 is >= ~$7.30, while the street implies ~12-13% growth. Measured against the reported FY26 $6.88, which includes the extra week, the street is only +8-9%. A reaffirm of 'double-digit' without a number reads at or below the street.

May 2026 +7.54% when FY27 double-digit was first set and the buyback raised (https://www.rttnews.com/3648058/disney-q2-profit-down-sees-earnings-growth-in-fy26-fy27-plans-at-least-8-bln-buyback-stock-up.aspx). evidence.why_not_priced: Previews quote '$7.91' as management's FY27 number (EW), a figure that is not in the company transcript. That suggests part of the market reads the plan as more aggressive than the company's 'double-digit' wording. If the gap were priced, previews would anchor on ~$7.30.
evidence.independence: CFO on 2026-09-09 repeated 'double-digit underlying growth in fiscal '27' without a number (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf). Same company, different document. Street figures: https://www.tikr.com/blog/disney-dis-stock-up-month-take-profits-or-buy-more.

evidence.text: A cost program sized after the last call could underpin the FY27 guide. Bloomberg (via Cord Cutters, 2026-11-02) reports Disney is preparing 'thousands' of job cuts, with some managers told to find 20% annual savings and parks, TV networks and studio carrying more. It follows a third layoff round on 2026-09-29, and on the Q3 call the CFO flagged 'meaningful reductions to cost, including labor and SG&A' with an update to come. Disney had ~231,000 employees.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2023 restructuring ($5.5B savings, ~7,000 jobs) was announced with Q1 FY23 results in Feb 2023 and the stock rose after hours. Its stock-level reaction is not in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The scale is unquantified ('planning stage'), so no savings number is in the street's FY27 $7.43-7.50. A dollar savings target on the call would be new. The caveat is built into the size: the CFO says savings will be redeployed into content, parks and tech, which caps how much reaches EPS.
evidence.independence: Q3 call (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf, CFO on cost reductions). 2026-09-29 layoff round (https://www.roic.ai/news/disney-cuts-hundreds-more-jobs-in-third-layoff-wave-of-2026-09-29-2026). The CFO on 2026-09-09 described a 'virtuous circle of reducing costs, reinvestment' (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf).

evidence.text: On 2026-09-09 the CFO said SVOD will now prioritise 'absolute OI dollar growth rather than just margins'. He also said Disney 'need[s] to invest more in content', with international content to go up 'by a lot on a percentage basis', and that margins will not go 'below double-digits'. That signals an FY27 DTC margin at or near FY26's ~double-digit level rather than expansion. Q3 SVOD margin was 13%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Streaming OI was the swing line in Feb 2026 (Q1 streaming OI +72%, stock -7.4% on overall guide/CEO news). There is no clean instance of a DTC-margin guide moving the stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: The CFO said it at a conference rather than in guidance, and previews still frame SVOD around the 13% margin and the double-digit target being 'within reach' (EW 2026-11-10). If it were priced, previews would model flat DTC margins for FY27. The CFO also said the spend 'won't be disruptive to the overall algorithm', which keeps this small.
evidence.independence: Same document as the cost-program and Avengers presales findings, which share the 2026-09-09 transcript (opposite or unrelated directions, both can be true). Q3 call: 'continued ... competitive in streaming ... pricing pressure' (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf).

evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the slate is public. The Q1 FY27 Entertainment comp is what management will guide to, and the Q1 FY26 base was weak (-35%) despite big films. If the market expected an easy Q1, previews would mention it. None found did.

next_guide.basis: This is the first FY27 guide. The street has FY27 about flat on FY26 ($3.31), but FY26 adj results include a $64.1m nine-month IEEPA refund COGS benefit (10-Q). Last year's first guide came in 7% under the street. The FY27 tailwinds are the end of Project Momentum cash costs, the APS brand transition (~$30m) and the absence of IEEPA tariffs. A guide below $3.34 at the midpoint is somewhat more likely than one above it, but this is not established.

evidence.text: The first FY27 guide lands against a street FY27 adj EPS of $3.34 ($3.30-3.39, 3 analysts), essentially flat on FY26's ~$3.31. FY26 adj results include a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit of $64.1m in COGS over nine months (~$0.70/share pre-offsets; part of it reverses tariffs paid in FY26 itself). Matching the street therefore needs real underlying growth in a battery category that management said worsened through Q3. Last year's first guide (FY26 $3.30-3.60, midpoint $3.45) was 7% under the $3.72 FactSet consensus.

evidence.why_not_priced: A consensus of $3.34 implies the street expects the company to replace a one-off refund with operating growth. If the market doubted that, the stock would not be 9% above the $22 mean target after a 25% run. The refund detail sits in the 10-Q's COGS note, not in the wire previews, which focus on the Q4 margin.

evidence.text: HUYA has fallen on 4 of its last 5 real earnings prints: Aug-2025 +4.53, Nov-2025 -4.29, Mar-2026 -8.96, May-2026 -5.79, Aug-2026 -1.65. The Aug-2026 drop came despite a non-GAAP EPS beat of 2x and a doubled buyback. The baseline's 8-row history also counts non-print 6-Ks (the 2026-11-05 share-plan amendment, the 2026-04-27 row, and the next-day +9.84 dividend/buyback session in March). Rebuilt from real prints, the median absolute move is about 4.5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue missed by about 1.7% and non-GAAP EPS beat, and the stock fell 1.65%. Q1 2026 fell 5.79%. Q4 2025 fell 8.96% before a +9.84% rebound when the special dividend and $50m buyback were announced.
evidence.why_not_priced: A reaction tendency is not a fact the price absorbs ahead of time. If the market expected relief, the stock would have outperformed KWEB into the print, and it matched KWEB to within a point over 5 and 20 days.
evidence.independence: Baseline move table (sealed) plus the Q2 bar/actual at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/HUYA ; the Mar-2026 dividend at https://www.barchart.com/story/news/787247/huya-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-announces-cash-dividend

evidence.text: Goose Goose Duck mobile, HUYA's co-published flagship and the main driver of its game-related segment (36.7% of Q2 revenue, +54% y/y), shows signs of fading. Kingsoft's executive put DAU at a 'stable 2-3 million' at end-July, against about 3 million on the Q4-2025 call. Limited-skin resale prices have collapsed (a 720-yuan gold skin resold at 350-450 in H1 and about 200 in H2). An analyst says the social-referral boom 'has run its course'. HUYA's own game segment grew only 1.7% q/q in Q2 (627.4m to 637.9m). The Q3 2025 base the segment laps (531.6m) has no GGD mobile, so y/y growth stays positive but should decelerate further.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Segment slowdown 69% to 54% in Q2 coincided with a revenue miss and a -1.65% reaction
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a Chinese-language trade-press story about Kingsoft and the game, and it does not mention HUYA. The only English preview (EW 11-10) still frames game publishing as the growth engine. If it were priced, HUYA would have lagged KWEB, and it did not.
evidence.independence: HUYA's own Q1/Q2 6-K segment numbers (627.4m, 637.9m) are a different document pointing the same way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1728190/000110465926094381/tm2622963d1_ex99-1.htm . The DAU and skin-price figures are proxies, not HUYA revenue.
evidence.link: Kingsoft Seasun is the exclusive licensor/operator of Goose Goose Duck mobile and HUYA is its joint publisher (TMTPost 2026-01-14, https://www.tmtpost.com/7842062.html). The game was HUYA's largest named driver of game-related revenue in Q1 and Q2 2026.

evidence.text: China's tipping-based live-streaming market kept shrinking. Kuaishou's live-streaming revenue fell 13.5% y/y in both Q1 and Q2 2026, after the CAC's 2026-04-13 notice on tipping (user-set caps, no ranking by tips alone, no rebate inducements) took full effect for Q3. HUYA's own live-streaming revenue fell much less (-3.3% in Q1, -4.5% in Q2, to RMB1,101.5m). Holding at -5% on the Q3 2025 base of about RMB1,157m gives about RMB1,099m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Live-streaming declines were reported in each of the last four quarters and are attributed to 'the industry environment'. No discrete reaction is separable.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the decline is in the consensus narrative. The unpriced part is whether the first full quarter under the April rule, plus HUYA's own streamer-contract trimming, makes the decline steeper than Q2's -4.5%.
evidence.independence: Kuaishou Q1/Q2 2026 live-streaming -13.5% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1185520551). HUYA's own series (Q2 6-K) is the broader and more direct number and shows a much milder decline, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.link: Same product (virtual-gift tipping on game/entertainment live streams in mainland China) under the same CAC rule; live streaming is about 63% of HUYA revenue. Kuaishou is a far broader platform, so transmission is partial.

evidence.text: On the 2026-08-11 call, the CEO said that 'since H2 began' HUYA has been proactively cutting streamer cooperation and contract costs to improve content ROI. Q3 is the first full quarter of those cuts. Gross margin had already risen from 13.5% to 14.7% and non-GAAP operating income from a loss to RMB16.2m in Q2, and Q2 non-GAAP EPS of RMB0.16 was double the RMB0.08 consensus. A further margin step is the most likely positive surprise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's large non-GAAP EPS beat still met a -1.65% reaction, so this name has not paid much for margin beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS was half the Q2 actual and the targets have not moved since 08-12. A priced margin story would show a stock holding up against KWEB, not tracking it to a 52-week low.
evidence.independence: Pedaily's account of the same results (https://news.pedaily.cn/202608/567559.shtml) reports the same H2 plan to 'refine streamer partnership and contract systems'. It is the same management statement, so this counts once. Cost cuts may also shrink live-streaming revenue (see the peer finding); that is revenue, this is margin.

evidence.text: The revenue bar of about RMB1.84bn (+9% y/y; single aggregator) needs game-related revenue of about RMB740-750m if live streaming lands near RMB1.10bn. That is +17% q/q, against +1.7% q/q in Q2. Q3 2025 did show a +28% q/q summer step in that segment (413.9m to 531.6m), so the bar is reachable only if that seasonality repeats while GGD fades. HUYA already missed the revenue bar in Q2 (RMB1.74bn vs 1.77bn).

The Q3 call is the natural place to name a launch date or pre-registration count, which is the only forward catalyst HUYA can offer without guidance. evidence.text: NBS household-appliance retail sales improved from deep declines in Q2 to roughly flat in Q3 2026 (July -1.9%, August +2.3%, September +1.9% y/y against June -8.7% and H1 -7.4%), against JD's Q2 electronics & home appliances revenue of -11.8% y/y; consensus (Guosen) already expects JD's electronics decline to narrow only to 'single digits'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Electronics was the line behind the Q2 revenue decline and the -7.3% reaction on 2026-08-13 (Caixin: 'subsidy pullback hits electronics sales', https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/jdcom-posts-first-quarterly-revenue-decline-as-subsidy-pullback-hits-electronics-sales-102473925.html).

If the market had read it as a full recovery, the revenue consensus would sit above management's 'retail back to slight growth' frame and the skew would not lean to puts.
evidence.independence: Proxy, macro-to-company. CONTRADICTED IN SIZE by the broader appliance-retail series AVC (all channels, cited by Haier as -10% in Q3 vs -12.4% in Q2), filed as the next finding; the two series disagree on how much appliances recovered, which is why this is sized small.

If priced, previews would be pencilling electronics close to flat rather than a single-digit decline.

evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by definition it is the market's expectation. The finding is that the bar is low relative to targets and to the last pre-print level, which favours an upside asymmetry only if the guide holds.

evidence.text: In 3 of the last 4 confirmed prints the stock fell sharply despite beating the quarter (Nov 2025 -9.3%, Feb 2026 about -22%, Aug 2026 -22.8%). The direction each time was set by forward guidance or profitability, and the one up print (May 2026 +20.3%) reiterated FY. The baseline's 8-event history mixes in non-earnings 6-Ks; the confirmed-print median absolute move is about 21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: History is not a forecast. The finding is that the reaction function has punished the guide more often than it rewarded the beat. The options price a 13% move, well below the realised ~21% median.
evidence.independence: Q3'25 -9.3%: https://www.tikr.com/blog/klarna-stock-sinks-over-9-despite-beating-consensus-estimates-in-q3. Aug 2026 -22.81% and May 2026 +20.31% are in the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: The Fed hiked in September 2026 (its first hike since 2023) and the ECB is also tightening. Klarna's funding cost was $171m, 0.47% of GMV, in Q2, with deposits at 88% of funding ($11.7bn, down from $13.0bn at December 2025). Higher deposit and benchmark rates pressure TMD and the fair-value adjustments on loans sold in H2.

evidence.text: The FY AOI guide of $280-300m, less H1 AOI of $159m and the Q3 guide of $5-15m, implies Q4 AOI of about $106-136m, the largest quarter by far. evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but the Q4 guide arrives tomorrow, and any slip of launches or merchant go-lives shows up as a Q4 AOI guide below the implied $106-136m. The Q3 AOI beat (finding 1) can offset this inside the FY range.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-09 MINISO disclosed Q3 Chinese-mainland GMV +25-30% YoY, driven by high-single-digit SSSG and faster than H1 (H1 China revenue +26.2%, Q2 +22.9%). That compares with a full-year China SSSG guide of low single digits (Capital Securities note) and an H2 China revenue guide of mid-double-digit. MINISO USA GMV was about +20% in Q3 and over +30% in September with positive SSSG. China is the profit engine: overseas was only 10-15% of profit in H1.

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: +5.8% on the day and consensus Q3 revenue (~+18%) sits above the guided H2 HSD. What may not be priced is the operating leverage of HSD China SSSG on the China margin. If it had been priced, the EPS consensus would have been revised up after Oct 9; AAII shows 1 down and 0 up in the last month.
evidence.independence: Capital Securities HK note restating the update against the FY low-single-digit China SSSG guide (https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5323354). Same underlying company document.

evidence.text: Guide arithmetic: FY26 revenue guided +mid-double-digit on FY25 RMB21.44bn implies H2 of about RMB13.2bn (+9%). Q3 at the Oct 9 run-rate (about RMB6.7-6.85bn, +16-18%) would leave Q4 at only +1-3% against a Q4'25 of about RMB6.25bn and a street Q4 of $1.07B (about RMB7.26bn). The FY revenue guide is therefore likely raised, or else Q4 is guided far below the street.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last guide change (Aug 28, a margin guide cut): HK shares -11%. Nov 2025: Q4 guided to +25-30% revenue and Deutsche Bank resumed Buy (https://www.itiger.com/news/2586286816).
evidence.why_not_priced: Street Q4 at $1.07B already sits above what the unchanged FY guide implies. A raise that only meets the street is partly priced. If a raise were fully expected, sell-side EPS revisions would be rising, not falling.
evidence.independence: FY25 revenue of RMB21.44bn from cbndata (https://www.cbndata.com/information/295167). H1 revenue from the company release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/miniso-group-announces-2026-june-quarter-and-interim-unaudited-financial-results-545636.shtml).

evidence.text: The EPS bar is split. Earnings Whispers has $0.37 and Benzinga $0.38, while AAII shows $0.32 from 2 analysts with 1 downward revision in the last month. The company's FY guide (adj net profit down high single digits, adj op margin -3-4pp, H1 adj NP -1.7%) implies H2 adj NP down about 13%. evidence.text: Overseas is in restructuring. The H2 overseas revenue guide is low-single-digit growth with distributor ('agency') revenue down double digits. The H2 plan nets 50-70 fewer overseas stores (100-110 distributor closures, 40-50 new direct stores). Inventory days rose from 214 to 273 in H1 and are to be cleared through promotions. The Oct 9 update said overseas was only 'largely in line' with guidance. Clearance and closure costs fall in Q3 overseas margin.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Overseas under-delivery was the core of the Aug 28 -11% reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Guided and therefore mostly priced. The open question is the margin cost of inventory clearance, which is not quantified anywhere. Net of the rest: China, which is 85-90% of profit, is running above guide (finding 1).

evidence.text: Yonghui (29.4% equity-accounted by MINISO) reported a Q3'26 attributable net loss of RMB82.7m, including a RMB76m fair-value loss on Advantage Solutions, on revenue down 8.3%. That implies a share of loss to MINISO of roughly RMB24m, if recognised without a lag. This is small, and far below the large Yonghui drag of 2025 (Q2'25 share of loss RMB136.9m), so GAAP net profit improves YoY below operating income.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025 Yonghui losses drove the 'net profit halved' headlines (https://www.itiger.com/news/1199486365) but the stock trades on adjusted figures.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is below operating income and excluded from adjusted net profit, so it reaches the stock only through GAAP headlines. Sized as a fraction.
evidence.independence: Q2'26 Yonghui share of loss of RMB17.2m in the company release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/miniso-group-announces-2026-june-quarter-and-interim-unaudited-financial-results-545636.shtml).

evidence.text: The Q3 revenue ramp rests on the Q2 account build. Ordering accounts rose from 30 (31 Mar) to 73 (30 Jun), out of about 175 transplant centres. Management said ordering frequency rose in Q2, distributor inventory held at about 1.5 weeks so there was no stocking, the permanent J-code took effect 1 Jul, and adults were about 75% of Q2 sales. Q3 is the first quarter with all 73+ accounts ordering. Against the $30.9M Earnings Whispers bar (+8% on $28.5M), the account base alone points to a beat; against the $35.5-38.0M figures elsewhere it is about at the bar.

evidence.why_not_priced: The bar is split: one aggregator asks only +8% QoQ while two others sit at $35.5-38M, so the market has no shared number. If the ramp were priced the stock would sit near its post-Q2 high of $21.24 and not at $17.23 with 17% of float short and puts bid. The CHMP drop in October took the stock down for a reason unrelated to US revenue.

evidence.text: On 2026-11-03 the CFO said Opera will set its 'final Q4 guidance with our typical prudence'. The FY guide of $734-742m implies Q4 revenue of $197.4-205.4m (+11-16% y/y, midpoint $201.4m) after a +20% Q3. The street's derived Q4 of about $203.4m (FY $740.0m) sits in the upper half of that range, so a 'prudent' Q4 guide is more likely to land at or below the street than above it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved this stock both ways. The initial FY26 guide plus a $300m buyback (2026-02-26) bought +23.38%. The FY raise with Q2 (2026-08-19) was sold -7.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The prudence remark has been public for two weeks, and the stock is roughly flat since 11-03 ($15.47 to $15.36), so some caution is in. But the street FY figure still sits at $740m, in the upper half of the range. If the market had priced a guide below the street, FY estimates would have come down toward the $738m midpoint. The StockAnalysis FY range ($735.8-744.4m) shows no such cut.
evidence.independence: Shares the 11-03 document with the Q3-deceleration finding. Independent support: the Q2 call transcript, where management said it built in a 'more normalized Q4 spike' (https://www.webull.com/news/15429727749776384), and Google's Q3 search slowdown (separate finding).

OPay had priced 16m ADSs at $19 (about $4bn valuation). Opera's 9.5% stake was carried at about $294.6m at YE2025 ($3.1bn valuation), roughly 22% of Opera's ~$1.36bn market cap. The 11-17 call is management's first chance to comment on the stake and the inquiry.

evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown (about $300m of market cap) is about equal to the whole OPay stake at its YE2025 carrying value, while the IPO was priced at a higher valuation than that carrying value and Bloomberg reports it is paused, not dead (weetracker 11-05). If the market saw the stake as merely delayed, the stock would sit nearer $17-18. The risk to this sign: the reported China inquiry runs through Zhou Yahui, also Opera's controlling shareholder via Kunlun, so part of the discount may be a China-link discount on Opera itself, which the call cannot remove. That caveat is why the finding is sized below 1.

evidence.text: Q4 new orders will compare against a $934M Q3 record (book-to-bill 3.0x) that included a one-off data-center award of more than $400M. Management said no further near-term projects above $400M are in the pipeline and that book-and-burn averages about $75M a quarter. Q4 orders are therefore likely to fall sequentially by half or more, and book-to-bill may land near 1.0-1.4x on revenue of about $330M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders are the line this name trades on. Q4 FY25: EPS beat by $0.44 and orders flat at $271M, stock -11.3%. Q3 FY26: record orders offset a revenue miss, -13.9% after hours recovered to -3.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sequential drop is foreseeable, and sophisticated holders should expect it. But the headline comparison (orders down about 50% q/q) is what the wire prints first, and on Q4 FY25 a weak order headline cost 11% despite a beat. If the market had fully discounted it, the November 2025 reaction would not have happened on a similar setup.

In FY26, 9-month net favorable contract-estimate changes fell to $12.8M from $15.1M, management flagged inflation in copper, aluminum, steel and engineered components plus SG&A pressure from standing up new facilities, and Q3 margin was 30.6%. A y/y margin decline in Q4 is likely.

evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.52-1.58 against $1.41 a year ago (split-adjusted) implies +8-12%, which needs margin to hold near 30-31% on +10-15% revenue. If the street had built in a closeout-free margin, EPS estimates would sit nearer $1.45.

evidence.text: Texas paused data-center approvals inside Powell's fiscal Q4. Gov. Abbott halted ERCOT grid-connection approvals (reported Aug 10) and TCEQ environmental permits from Sep 21. On Nov 3, governor-elect Hinojosa won on a promised moratorium on all new data-center approvals; Texas is cited as about 30% of US projects. Powell is Houston-based, commercial & other industrial (incl. data center) is 40% of its backlog, and its 10-Q lists data-center legislation as a risk factor. The Q4 order intake and the call's data-center pipeline commentary will be read through this.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Powell print with a data-center policy shock. The Nov 4-5 sector sell-off took POWL to its $121 low.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the whole power complex sold off on it Nov 4-5 and POWL with it. What is unpriced is Powell's own exposure, which the company has not quantified. Its $400M+ award spans 'at least five North American facilities' with no location given. This is a proxy, not a company confirmation, and is sized small. Net of the rest: oil & gas, utility (24% of backlog) and petrochemical (30% with O&G) are untouched by it.
evidence.independence: Texas Tribune on Hinojosa's pledge: https://texastribune.org/2026/11/04/data-center-texas-pause-gina-hinojosa-governor-policies/ ; Tikr on the Nov 5 sell-off ('forced control on CapEx'): https://www.tikr.com/blog/vertiv-sinks-another-16-as-data-center-selloff-deepens-forced-control-on-capex

evidence.text: Peers and competitors that reported the same Jul-Sep quarter after Powell last spoke all showed accelerating electrical demand. Eaton's electrical data-center orders more than doubled on a rolling 12-month basis, its electrical backlog was about $20.4B (+46%), and it raised FY26 EPS guidance. Vertiv's organic orders more than doubled and it raised guidance (Oct 28). Hubbell's data-center sales rose more than 80% and its utility T&D/substation backlog kept building (Oct 27).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured as a read-through for POWL. Powell's Q3 record orders coincided with strong peer data-center demand.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer prints are public, and POWL fell anyway on the policy scare, so the market has chosen policy over demand evidence. If the peer read had been carried into POWL, its 20-day return would not be -8.5%. Sized small because peer data center demand is not Powell's order book.
evidence.independence: Eaton: https://fourweekmba.com/ai-eaton-filing-electrical-backlog-reaches-20-4b-up-46/ ; Vertiv: https://datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/vertiv-shares-jump-14-percent-as-data-center-earnings-beat-expectations
evidence.link: Same products and end markets: Eaton is a direct competitor in switchgear and power distribution for data centers and utilities; Hubbell sells utility substation/T&D equipment into the same utility capex that is 24% of Powell's backlog; Vertiv sells data-center power gear into the same hyperscale projects. The street FY is about $157M. The company's IR list shows no order or contract release between the Aug 6 call and Nov 16, only product, partnership and M&A releases (Oct 1, 12, 19, 22, Nov 2). Red Cat cut its FY2025 guide from $80-120M to $34.5-37.5M in the Q3 2025 release.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue consensus is $38.8-40.7M, nearly double Q2's $20.2M. Q3 revenue estimates were cut 15.7% over three months. Northland cut its Q3 EPS estimate to -$0.28 from -$0.22 on Sept 16, below the -$0.20 consensus. Red Cat missed revenue consensus in Q2 2026 ($20.2M vs $22.65M) and Q3 2025 ($9.6M vs $16.7M).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: an 11% revenue miss with the guide held bought +6.23%. Q3 2025: a 42% miss with a guide cut gave -10%. The quarter alone has not moved this stock; the guide has.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the estimate cuts and the whisper (-$0.23) show the street already leans to a miss. Consensus still sits at almost 2x Q2 revenue.
evidence.independence: Chartmill revision data (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/1RCAT.MI/estimates) and the Earnings Whispers preview, separate sources.

evidence.text: Teal Drones (Red Cat) missed the order-eligible leaderboard at Gauntlet I (March 2026; 11 winners, about 30,000 drones worth up to $150M) and at Gauntlet II (results Sept 15-18; 10 winners, about 60,000 drones). The $14-28M of potential Q3 Drone Dominance revenue that the Earnings Whispers preview says was floated therefore has no sourced order behind it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line. The stock fell through late September after the Gauntlet II leaderboard.
evidence.why_not_priced: The leaderboards are public and the stock fell on them, so this is mostly priced. It is still filed because the 2026-11-10 preview treats Drone Dominance as a possible Q3 contributor, so some estimates may embed it.
evidence.independence: Gauntlet I: DroneXL 2026-03-06 says Teal did not place (https://dronexl.co/2026/03/06/drone-dominance-program-gauntlet-1-winners/). The Fool 2026-10-03 says Red Cat appears 'knocked out, at least for now' (https://fool.com/investing/2026/10/03/heres-who-won-the-drone-dominance-gauntlet-2-conte).

evidence.text: Mitch McDonald, Red Cat's UAS division CEO, said on Aug 14, after the Aug 6 call, that Army funding is 'very spotty', that appropriations arrive late and that 'they can't commit to anything for any program'. He cited the Army's $52M March order for over 2,500 Skydio X10D as the Army keeping competition alive on SRR.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Army was 73% of FY2025 revenue and about half of H1 2026 (10-Q: Customer A 51% of H1). When Army timing slipped in 2025 the FY guide was cut.
evidence.why_not_priced: It ran in a trade outlet, not on the wire. Consensus FY still at $157M shows estimates did not mark down Army timing.
evidence.independence: The 10-Q risk factor on government revenue timing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/748268/000162828026054368/rcat-20260630.htm). Same direction as the guide finding; a separate statement.

evidence.text: On Nov 5 at Euronaval, Blue Ops (Red Cat's USV unit, which management said would be profitable by Q4) was described as 'seeking to turn overseas interest into orders'. No named customer or order appeared, and the B-26 is in full-rate production without a disclosed buyer.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Blue Ops first revenue was reported in Q2 with no split. The preview notes Blue Ops' first-year framing has already been scaled back.
evidence.why_not_priced: Paywalled trade press. The Q4 street at $73.6M implicitly needs USV deliveries that have no announced customer.
evidence.independence: WorkBoat 2026-09-24 reports the Variant 7 ramp with no orders or customers named (https://www.workboat.com/blue-ops-ramps-variant-7-usv-production-at-georgia-facility).

evidence.text: FY2027 Pentagon funding runs on a CR through Dec 11, 2026, at FY2026 levels with no new starts and no new multi-year contracts, and a funding lapse is possible from Dec 12. That delays Q4 award timing for a company whose H2 depends on government awards.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to RCAT.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a widely known macro fact, but the company has not said how the CR affects its Q4. It is a proxy: SRR is an existing program, and existing programs can continue under a CR.
evidence.independence: Proxy. ClearanceJobs 2026-10-01 (https://news.clearancejobs.com/2026/10/01/the-pentagon-starts-fiscal-2027-on-a-stopgap-heres-how-it-affects-defense-jobs/) and McDonald's 'funding very spotty' remark.

evidence.text: Red Cat agreed on Oct 21 to buy Steyr Motors for EUR 39/share in cash (5,251,261 shares, about EUR 205M, roughly $240M), 'fully financed'. June 30 cash was $325.6M and H1 operating cash outflow $78.7M (about $39M a quarter). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May 2026 $225M offering at $9.40, 15% below market, sent the stock lower (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Red+Cat+slides+on+$225+million+discounted+stock+offering).
evidence.why_not_priced: What the money buys: engines for the Blue Ops USVs (vertical integration). The tender is not a demand signal, and Blue Ops has no announced orders, so the outlay does not corroborate a ramp. A disclosed raise or facility on the call is not priced. The deal itself is public since Oct 19.
evidence.independence: Steyr's own ad-hoc release (https://ir.steyr-motors.com/en/finanzmitteilungen/ad-hoc-en/); the 10-Q cash walk (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/748268/000162828026054368/rcat-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: The 10-Q at June 30, 2026 shows inventory incl. prepaid of $84.8M against $30.4M at year-end, alongside contract liabilities and deposits of only $0.26M and receivables down to $9.5M from $26.2M. The company has built stock for an H2 ramp, but no customer has prepaid against it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Inventory conversion has not been a reported line before.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deposit and receivable figures sit in the 10-Q notes, not the release. An inventory build of $54M at a 16% gross margin is enough material for about $60M+ of revenue, which supports the capacity to ship if orders come. It is mixed evidence, so it is sized small and positive.
evidence.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview flags the same inventory as needing to turn. Same document as the guide arithmetic, different lines.

A Q3 revenue figure near $18-25m matters less than those.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q4 2026 revenue $88.6m (Benzinga earnings-forecasts page, snippet_only, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SHAZ/earnings-forecasts)
next_guide.street_full_year: FY2026 revenue $118.6m (range $88.1-151.6m, 5 analysts) and FY2027 $1.54bn (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/shaz/forecast/)
next_guide.company_current_guide: No numeric guide. Qualitative only: 'revenue expected to ramp materially from Q3 2026 through 2027' (Q2 release, 2026-08-06), and on the Q2 call 'the first material revenue to commence in Q4 2026 as large-scale B300 and GB300 deployments come online'. Target of more than 68,000 GPUs by mid-2027, raised from 64,000 on 2026-10-01.
next_guide.basis: The company has never given a numeric guide, so a 'maintain the qualitative ramp' is the base case. The risk is a slip: the 6 Nov report of management's late-October update says 9 halls were energised, 2 were due in November and 1 was still under construction, and the CEO named data-centre readiness and hardware delivery as the ramp risks. Against that, the GPU target was raised on 1 Oct and a $356m GPU facility was signed for a customer contract.

evidence.text: The real bar is low. The stock fell from $48.12 (2026-10-06) to $19.86 (2026-11-16), down 59% and 12% on the print day itself. That puts market cap at about $760m on 38.34m shares (13D/A share count), against $1.9bn of cash at June 30 and ~$1.04bn face of convertible notes. The press attributes the fall to 'potential data center delays' and a 'funding gap', without a named source or company disclosure. A release that shows clusters billing and cash covering the build clears the bar the market holds, which is far below the stale $105 mean target.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is only one prior print as a listed company with results on record (Q2, 2026-08-06), and it was sold: about -5% on 08-07, with -57% drift since. The name gave back a +13% sympathy rally on CoreWeave within two sessions (11-11 to 11-13).
evidence.why_not_priced: The price is the expectation itself, so this finding is about what the price assumes, not about an unseen fact. The size is small because the skew (+32 vol points, downside paid) says the option market expects more downside. If the market had priced a clean Q4 ramp, the stock would sit nearer its $48 level from early October.
evidence.independence: Cause of the fall per press: https://cryptobriefing.com/sharonai-holdings-shares-plunge-52-percent/ (2026-11-04). Share count from the 13D/A: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2068385/000093583626000500/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml. Cash at Q2 from https://quartr.com/events/sharonai-holdings-inc-shaz-q2-2026_FRcIPO5A. Q3 capex has consumed an unknown share of that cash, which is why the size is small.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue is likely to land at or below the disputed bar ($18.3m Earnings Whispers, $25.3m Benzinga). On the Q2 call (2026-08-06) the CEO said Q3 carries only 'a full month and a bit of billing' for the B300 cluster handed over in July, and that 'the first material revenue' commences in Q4. Q3 upside depends on the $950m customer's first phase (accepted 2026-08-20, revenue 'phased across Q3 and Q4') and on ESDS's 8,200-GPU B300 cluster, whose delivery was due 16 Sep. I found no confirmation that ESDS went live, and short seller Bleecker Street (30 Apr) questioned ESDS's capacity to pay. My read: about $15-20m, so roughly -8% against $18.3m and a clear miss against $25.3m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 revenue of $1.93m against ~$7.5m consensus was sold: about -5% on 2026-08-07, then -57% drift.
evidence.why_not_priced: The two estimate sources disagree, so the street may still carry a $25m number that management never endorsed. If the market had priced a Q3 miss, the higher estimate would have been cut to match the Earnings Whispers figure. Capped small because the bar is disputed and the company already told the market material revenue comes in Q4, so a miss lands inside what management said.
evidence.independence: The $950m acceptance is from a separate company release: https://finviz.com/news/384019/sharon-ai-successfully-delivers-ai-cloud-deployment-for-global-technology-customer (2026-08-20). ESDS timing: https://convergedigest.com/sharon-ai-planss-8k-b300-gpu-cluster-in-australia/ (2026-04-02). Bleecker Street on ESDS: https://bollwerk.ai/blog/shaz-bleecker-street-short-report/ (2026-05-01).

evidence.text: The Q4 ramp the street models ($88.6m Q4, $118.6m FY2026, so H2 needs about $115m against $1.9m in Q2) is exposed to energisation timing. Per a 6 Nov report of management's late-October update, 212 MW is secured across 12 AU/NZ sites and 120 MW is contracted, but grid power reaches the data hall at only 9 sites, 2 halls were scheduled for November and 1 was still under construction. The CEO named 'hardware delivery and data center readiness' as the two ramp risks. A Q4 or 2027 timing push is the main way this print disappoints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 call reframed 'material revenue' from Q3 to Q4, and the stock fell after the release (about -5% on 08-07). There is no numeric-guide history.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 $88.6m and the $105 targets have not moved with the stock, so the sell-side has not cut. If the market fully priced a slip, the remaining 'delay' fear would show up as estimate cuts, and none are visible. The stock's 59% fall and the +32 skew say much of it is already in the price, and short float is 14.5%, so the size is moderate.
evidence.independence: Same concern stated by the CEO on the Q2 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2951556, 2026-08-06) and by the press (https://cryptobriefing.com/sharonai-holdings-shares-plunge-52-percent/, 2026-11-04). The halls detail rests on one German secondary source, and no 8-K for the late-October update was found on EDGAR.

evidence.text: After Q3 (8-K filed 2026-10-01, agreement dated 28 Sep), two subsidiaries signed up to $356m of senior secured, GPU-backed SPV term loans at 7.25-9.95% fixed. The loans are 42-month bullet maturities with a limited, releasable parent guarantee that becomes non-recourse once Facility A is repaid. Proceeds buy servers and GPUs for a named customer compute contract. Management called it the first of a series and raised the target to more than 68,000 GPUs by mid-2027, from 64,000. That is non-dilutive funding for contracted demand and answers part of the 'funding gap' narrative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the announcement the stock went from $54.60 (09-30) to $48.12 (10-06) and then collapsed in mid-October, so the market did not reward it at the time.
evidence.why_not_priced: The facility is public. What is not yet visible is whether the call frames it as closing the funding gap, together with Q3-end cash after capex. The October sell-off on 'funding gap' fears came after this facility was announced, which suggests the market has not credited it. Sized small because financing only matters through the ramp it buys.
evidence.independence: Company release: https://finviz.com/news/397531/sharon-ai-enters-into-gpu-backed-debt-facility-expanding-funding-flexibility-for-ai-factory-deployments (2026-10-01). Same event, so these are one fact.

evidence.text: The first phase of the 5-year, ~$950m contract with a 'global technology company' was delivered and accepted by the customer on 2026-08-20, which also triggered release of cash security from escrow. Revenue on it was stated to start phased across Q3 and Q4 2026. At full run-rate the contract is ~$190m a year, ~$16m a month. This is a real billing source inside Q3 beyond the July cluster.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate history; contract announcements have been sold or faded (a 22% fall on 2026-07-28 in the week of the $1.32bn contract, per Quiver).
evidence.why_not_priced: The release gave no GPU count and no billing amount, so nobody can size the Q3 contribution. It may be why one consensus source sits at $25m. This only offsets part of the Q3-revenue finding above. It is a different document, but both findings land on the same line.
evidence.independence: Q2 call: Q3 billing is 'a month and a bit' on the July cluster (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2951556), which points the other way on Q3 magnitude.

evidence.why_not_priced: Headline EPS scrapers may print a large 'beat' after hours. Below operating income, with no path to the guide, so [sizing note removed].

evidence.text: Expectations are deeply reset. Spot $8.825 is 53% below the 52-week high, about 60% down over a year (Simply Wall St, 2026-11-03: $22.31 to $8.91), about 8.3x forward earnings (debelegger), and far below the ~$15 mean target. The stock went into the print -5.9% over five sessions, so the bar the market holds is lower than in August.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A low starting multiple did not stop the selling: the stock was already about $9-10 before the Q2 print and still fell 11.9%. The post-Q2 drift was +4.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The low multiple is itself the price. The finding is that the bar for a relief move is lower than at any print in the past year. If the market expected another leg down, the 5-day pre-print selloff would have pushed the stock back to the $7.74 October low and put/call OI would be skewed well above 1.11.
evidence.independence: Valuation from https://www.debelegger.nl/en/stock/TME.US (forward P/E 8.3) and Benzinga's price history https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TME/charts (down 55% over a year, low $7.74 on Oct 2). Separate sources, same price series.

evidence.text: On confirmed releases (not the baseline's 6-K matcher), TME has sold three of its last four prints by 9.6-25%: Q3 2025 beat then -9.64% intraday; Q4 2025 guide miss -25%; Q1 2026 in line about -1.3%; Q2 2026 slight beat (revenue +$20m, EPS +$0.01) -11.92%. A consensus beat alone has not been bought.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: headline beats on 2025-11-12 and 2026-08-11 were both sold by about 10-12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Reaction history is not a fact about this quarter. It is a sign that holders sell this name on what the quarter reveals about core growth. Only a full-quarter Ximalaya headline beat would make this print look different, and that is exactly the kind of beat holders have discounted. If the market had decided the derating was over, the implied move would be well below the name's ~10% realised print moves rather than 9.2%.
evidence.independence: Q4 2025 -25%: https://www.itiger.com/news/2620285775; Q3 2025 -9.64%: https://www.itiger.com/news/1123949293; Q2 2026 -11.92%: sealed baseline. Separate events.

evidence.text: Arithmetic on company figures: Ximalaya added RMB407m in the 43 days after the 2026-05-18 close, about RMB0.85-0.9bn at that run-rate for a full Q3. Ex-Ximalaya revenue grew about 1% in Q2 (RMB8.52bn vs RMB8.44bn). Q3 therefore lands near RMB9.3-9.4bn against the $1.35bn consensus (~RMB9.17bn at the 6.79 convenience rate): a headline revenue beat of roughly 1-2%, mostly inorganic.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat by about 1.3% with the stock -11.9%; Q3 2025 beat with the stock -9.6%. Revenue beats have not paid on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Earnings Whispers preview already calls Ximalaya's contribution 'flattering math'. The RMB conversion of the USD consensus is uncertain, so the size of any headline beat is too. If the full-quarter Ximalaya step-up were not already in the bar, consensus would sit near Q2's +6% growth rather than +8-13%.
evidence.independence: The Q2 Ximalaya figure and the ~1% organic growth are confirmed independently by https://m.jiemian.com/article/15077937.html. The consensus figure comes from the Earnings Whispers preview.

evidence.text: QuestMobile June 2026 (reported around 2026-09-10/15): Soda Music MAU 167m (+68.7% y/y) is approaching QQ Music's 189m (-0.7% y/y, down from +6.1% in March). Kugou fell -10.7% y/y (worse than March's -6.3%), Kuwo -18.5%, Quanmin K Ge -29.7%. Traffic erosion at TME's light-user apps accelerated through the end of Q2, which pressures ad-supported revenue and light-user membership in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 print (-25%) turned on falling MAU and competition. The Q2 2026 call conceded ad headwinds and light-user pressure, and the stock fell 11.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: TME stopped disclosing MAU and paying users in 2026, so third-party traffic data is the only window on the core, and it is not on terminals. Against that, the competition story is widely known and the stock is at lows. If the market had fully priced accelerating erosion, the stock would not have drifted +5% after Q2. This is a proxy, not company data, and SVIP/high-value users were said to be unaffected.
evidence.independence: The same QuestMobile June data appears at https://www.lanjinger.com/d/1789013592290576849 (2026-09-15), but both articles rest on one dataset. The March data at https://www.36kr.com/p/3796235964243201 shows the trend.

evidence.text: The 2026-08-11 call set a cautious H2 frame with no numeric guide: CFO said H2 gross margin will be 'decreasing slightly year-over-year', FY net margin 'will go down slightly' with EBITDA up, sales and operating expenses up slightly, and the ad-supported model 'experienced some headwinds'. No numeric Q4 guide is likely, and the cautious tone is likely to continue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The March 2026 guide miss (Q1 ~5% and FY ~2% below consensus) cost about 25%. The August cautious margin commentary went with -11.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Most of this sits inside what management already guided to, which is why it is sized small. What is not priced is any H2 margin decline steeper than 'slight', or a first 2027 comment. If the market expected a clean outlook, the targets would not have stayed reset at $12-13 since March.
evidence.independence: The same call is summarised at https://statementdog.com/analysis/TME/earnings_calls/317107 (one document). The FY guide miss is at https://www.itiger.com/news/2620285775.

evidence.text: Capital return capacity is high and management has signalled more. On 2026-08-11 the CFO said 'we're also preparing for another round of share buyback'. $600m remains under the $1bn 2025 program, which runs to March 2027 ($400m used, all in Q2 at about $9.2/ADS). Cash and investments were RMB44.2bn at June 30, and TME raised $1bn of 5.05%/5.65% notes in September 2026 for general corporate purposes. A new program announced with Q3 is plausible; $1bn would be roughly 7-8% of the market cap.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $1bn 2025 program was announced with Q4 2024 results in March 2025 and the shares rose (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/encent-music-shares-rise-after-q4-earnings-beat/ch7kBUGRb23; the date is inferred from context). The Q2 2026 completion of $400m did not prevent -11.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Intent is public, but the size and timing are not. The notes raise debt capacity well beyond operating needs with RMB44bn of cash already in hand, which points to returns or M&A. If a large new buyback were priced, the stock would not be trading near Q2's average repurchase price of $9.2. The financing question has been asked: the proceeds are for general purposes, with no distress signal (the prospectus says 'no material adverse change' since June 30), so the notes are read as a positive or a zero.
evidence.independence: The $1bn notes are in the 424B2 dated 2026-09-03 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001744676/000119312526382909/d87523d424b2.htm). Cash and the Q2 buyback are in the Q2 6-K. Earnings Whispers also notes management 'hinted at a new shareholder return program' (https://finviz.com/news/420443/tencent-music-must-show-its-core-subscription-engine-can-outrun-ximalayas-flattering-math).

evidence.text: Mid-quarter statement: TME's 424B2 for the $1bn notes, dated 2026-09-03 (two months into Q3), states 'There has been no material adverse change in the financial or trading position of the Company since June 30, 2026.' This is the only company statement on Q3 trading found between the Aug 11 call and the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is boilerplate in a bond prospectus that equity holders rarely read. It rules out a Q3 collapse through early September but says nothing about growth. If the market feared a Q3 breakdown, the October low would have been retested into the print.
evidence.independence: This is the same document as the notes in the capital finding (one 424B2), but a different fact.

evidence.text: QQ Music's official notice (2026-05-12) raised the list price of the Deluxe Green Diamond monthly card from RMB20 to RMB25, but promotional prices stayed unchanged and IT Home found the actual monthly card still at RMB20. ARPPU support in Q3 is minimal.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier ARPPU-led membership growth (2024-25) did not protect the Q3 2025 print (-9.6%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The change is a list-price adjustment only, so there is little to price. If effective prices had risen, membership growth guidance would have been raised in August, and it was not.
evidence.independence: https://m.sohu.com/a/1021558056_122004016/ reports the same notice (one underlying notice).

evidence.text: Peer: NetEase Cloud Music Q2 2026 revenue was roughly flat y/y at RMB2.0bn (H1 +3.4%), with membership growth offset by 'monthly ARPPU dilution due to changes in the subscriber mix'. Industry pricing pressure from free/cheap tiers is visible at the number-two subscription player.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: TME's Q2 2026 print, with membership growth slowing to 8% including Ximalaya, fell 11.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a Q2 data point published in August, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it is the only direct-competitor subscription read available, and it shows ARPPU dilution rather than price gains.
evidence.independence: The NetEase release at https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3944574/netease-announces-second-quarter-and-interim-2026-unaudited-financial-results is the same numbers in another document.
evidence.link: Direct competitor in Chinese online music subscriptions, same product and the same users being contested by Soda Music. NetEase Cloud Music revenue is about a quarter of TME's music revenue. It reported Q2, not Q3, so this is a stale read-through.

evidence.text: Counterparty: Universal Music Group's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-29) showed organic subscription revenue growth of +9.5% against an ~8.2% analyst estimate, helped by wholesale price increases ('Streaming 2.0'). Global subscription monetisation is healthy, but UMG gave no China or TME-specific figure.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of TME reacting to a UMG print found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Out-of-market read-through. For a supplier, rising wholesale prices are, if anything, a cost item for TME. The size is near zero because no figure links it to TME's quarter.
evidence.independence: The earnings-call detail at https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/supercharged-downtowns-margins-and-more-cost-cuts-what-i-learned-from-umgs-q3-earnings/ comes from the same company event.
evidence.link: UMG licenses its recorded-music catalogue to TME (a supplier of content). The China share of UMG subscription revenue is not disclosed, and UMG's growth is driven mostly by Western DSP price rises, so the transmission to TME is weak.

evidence.text: The FY2026 annual dividend is normally declared with the Q4 results in March (FY2025: $0.24/ADS, ~$370m, declared 2026-03-17 per the 424B2). Any dividend increase resolves then, not at this print, unless a special distribution is announced on 2026-11-17.

evidence.text: China's smartphone market shrank 15.4% y/y in Q3 2026 to about 57.9m units (IDC, 2026-10-13), accelerating from H1, as memory costs forced OEM price rises. Xiaomi was down 20.4% and OPPO and vivo fell sharply. Handsets are a core Weibo ad vertical that already declined in Q2, and management said on the Q2 call it was 'less optimistic' for Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 handset ad decline (flagged in the release) arrived alongside a -1.32% day. No separate line reaction is identifiable.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management pre-warned on handsets, and the street's -11.5% cc implied bar plausibly already carries a weak handset vertical. What may not be priced is the depth: a 15% unit decline with OEM margin squeeze points to deeper ad cuts than 'less optimistic' implies. Net of the rest: auto, internet services and AI app promotion grew in Q2 and have to offset it.
evidence.independence: Omdia: shipments -12%, lowest Q3 since 2013 (https://omdia.tech.informa.com/pr/2026/oct/mainland-china-smartphone-shipments-drop-to-lowest-q3-level-since-2013). This is an industry proxy; the company has not quantified handset ad revenue.

evidence.text: China passenger-car retail fell 28% y/y in September 2026 (CPCA final, 1.618m units) and 21.7% YTD, with NEV retail -16.7%. Automobile was the vertical Weibo said would show 'continued strength in the second half' on frequent NEV launches.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto advertising grew in Q2 2026 despite a weak 2026 car market (YTD retail already down), so retail volumes have not transmitted to Weibo's auto ad line so far.
evidence.why_not_priced: Car makers fighting for share in a shrinking market often keep launch marketing high, so transmission to ad spend is ambiguous; it is filed small. If the market had priced an auto-ad cut, management's 'continued strength' would already have been questioned in analyst notes, and none found does so.
evidence.independence: Steelorbis CPCA preliminary -24%: https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/cpca-chinas-passenger-vehicle-retail-sales-down-24-in-september-2026-1482872.htm. Macro proxy, not confirmed by the company.

evidence.text: Alibaba, Weibo's largest single advertiser, described its September 2025 quarter as the peak of its quick-commerce investment and said intensity would fall significantly afterwards. Weibo's Alibaba ad revenue was $45.5m (+112%) in Q3 2025 against $39.2m (+10%, on AI app promotion) in Q2 2026. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, when Alibaba ad more than doubled while non-Alibaba fell 13%: reaction not reliably sourced (only templated mirror pages). No measured reaction on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management flagged the base and the $415m consensus reconciles with Alibaba ad falling ~40%. The residual is that Alibaba's Qwen/AI-app promotion (which lifted Q2) may hold the line better than the consensus arithmetic assumes; the sign could flip, so it is sized small. Alibaba's own September-2026-quarter results were not found before this print.
evidence.independence: Weibo Q3 2025 release for the base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1595761/000110465925113392/tm2531299d1_ex99-1.htm. Weibo Q2 2026 call on e-commerce pressure: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WB/Q22026.

evidence.text: Management's only forward statement (Q2 call, 2026-08-19) was cautious: Q3 factors 'expected to put some pressure on year-over-year advertising revenue growth', the consumer recovery 'will take longer', and competition for ad budgets stays intense. With handset and car data deteriorating through the quarter, the Q4 commentary is more likely to extend the decline than to call a turn, against a street Q4 of $448.6m (-5.2% reported, about -11% cc).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q2 call, with the same cautious tone, the stock fell 1.32% and made a new 12-month low within two sessions; Citi downgraded the same week.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 already embeds a sharp cc decline, so a 'pressure continues' tone is mostly priced. The risk is a quantified statement (e.g. Q4 ad down double digits cc) or a margin warning, which this name has not given before. Shrunk for the crowded short.
evidence.independence: Yahoo Q4 consensus: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WB/analysis/. Handset and auto data in findings 4 and 5 share this direction but are separate documents. The transcript is auto-generated and partly garbled.

evidence.text: Weibo has a US$200m buyback authorised through 2026-12-31, about 13% of the ~$1.48bn market cap at $6.04 (245.67m shares), funded from cash. evidence.why_not_priced: Execution is unknown. GuruFocus shows zero buyback through Q1 2026, which, if accurate, means the authorisation has been idle. A disclosed acceleration would be new information, and an idle program is no change, so the size is small and positive.

evidence.text: Yalla gave the identical Q3 guide ($78-85m) a year ago and printed $89.6m, 5.4% over the top. Q3 is seasonally its strongest quarter (Q3 2025 $89.6m vs Q2 2025 $84.6m, +5.9%), and Q2 2026 already beat its top at $82.6m. Applying last year's Q2-to-Q3 step gives about $87.5m, above the $85m top and about at the single-source street $87.2m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarters that beat the guide top: +4.12% (Q2 2026) and +1.0% (Q3 2025). Quarters inside the guide: -6.65% (Q1 2026) and -8.3% (Q4 2025). The stock punishes 'inside guide' more than it rewards 'above'.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the street $87.2m already sits above the guide top. What is not priced is a number at or above $88-90m, a repeat of last year's 5% over-delivery; if the market expected that, the stock would not trade at about net cash.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 guide and actual from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36033942/yalla-group-limited-announces-unaudited-third-quarter-2025-financial-results); a different document from the Q2 2026 release.

evidence.text: Gulf non-oil activity recovered through Q3 despite the ongoing Iran war: the UAE PMI was 55.3 in both August and September (a 20-month high), and Saudi Arabia's rose from 53.8 to 55.3 with new orders at their fastest since February. Management said on 2026-08-17 that sequential MAU growth would resume in Q3. Together these point to paying users (10.9m in Q2 vs 11.2m) stabilising after the war-driven drop.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Paying-user declines blamed on 'geopolitical events' came with the -6.65% (Q1 2026) and -8.3% (Q4 2025) reactions; the Q2 rebound in flagship products came with +4.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: A business PMI is a proxy for spending on social apps, and the company has not confirmed the link. The stock fell 3.4% over 20 days rather than rising, so the market has not credited a regional recovery.
evidence.independence: Proxy. The management MAU remark is on the Q2 call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262114446-tradingkey); the war is still described as ongoing (Hormuz attacks).

evidence.text: Management reiterated on 2026-08-17 that FY2026 revenue would be 'broadly in line' with FY2025 ($341.9m). With H1 at $161.6m, that needs about $180m in H2, roughly $93m in Q4 if Q3 prints about $87m. That matches the single-source street Q4 of $93.5m, while Yalla's Q4 guides have historically been ranges like $78-85m. A Q4 guide midpoint in the high $80s would leave FY at about -1 to -2% and below the street's Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: beat top by 5% but guided Q4 at $78-85m, below the Q3 actual, and the stock only rose +1.0%. Q4 2025 print with the first FY-flat guide: -8.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed the FY-flat guide and the $93.5m street Q4, the stock would not sit about at net cash. So a soft Q4 guide is partly priced, which is why this is sized small; a strong Q4 guide (SLG major version, Turbo Match monetisation) is the upside case.
